name: Master Students
description: Cheap and enthusiastic workforce, they can save you a lot of work.

name: PhD Students
description: They decided to do a PhD. Now they are working hard.

name: Postdocs
description: These brilliant minds are here only to serve your needs.

name: Research Fellows
description: You pay them a lot. They work a lot.

name: Permanent Staff
description: Somebody who gets a permanent position in physics has to be good.

name: Tenured Professors
description: They bring their own group along and are able to get a lot of work done.

name: Nobel Laureates
description: They received their prize for a reason.

name: Summer Students
description: Their best ideas come between two parties.

name: Citizen Scientists
description: Thousands of volunteers lend their computers' spare time to analyse your data.

name: Collaboration Spokespersons
description: They speak for thousands of physicists and somehow get them all to agree.

name: Directors-General
description: They run the whole laboratory, and the whole laboratory runs faster.

name: Engineers
description: They keep thousands of magnets cold and the beam on track.

name: Data Scientists
description: They teach machines to find one interesting event in a billion.

name: Theorists
description: They explain your results, ideally before you get them.

name: Parallel Selves
description: Other versions of you, from the universes next door. They already know the tricks.

name: Boltzmann Brains
description: Minds that fluctuated out of pure noise. Surprisingly good at data analysis.

name: Universe Builders
description: They choose the laws of physics for new universes, and test them in yours.

name: Shift Crew
description: They watch the detector around the clock, so you can sleep.

name: Technicians
description: They know where every one of the detector's hundred thousand cables goes.

name: Accelerator Operators
description: From the CERN Control Centre, they steer the beams around the ring.

name: Astronauts
description: They service your particle detector on the International Space Station.
